brief: `drawPuddles` is the most expensive live pass in the town — 0.94 ms of a 2.0 ms frame at peak rain — and it draws every one of the 792 pools whatever the camera is doing, so at a quarter camera most of that work lands off-frame. The cost of not culling is already measured for you (`probes/pool-cost.mjs`: drawPuddles 0.221 -> 0.308 ms, wet frame +5.5%), which is why this is a 25-minute job and not an investigation. Cull to the visible frame and give the budget back. This is a Harness brief: it changes nothing a viewer sees and does not count toward the lane's balance — the point is that b130 is about to make the roofline more expensive and there is a measured 0.9 ms sitting in a loop that mostly draws things nobody can see.
successLooksLike: `perf.mjs` (or frame-cost) shows drawPuddles materially cheaper at the four quarter cameras on a wet frame, and byte-identical output: hash the canvas at pinned instants at every framing on both builds and show ZERO changed pixels. Closes c189 and c199.
avoid: A cull is only free if it is exact — cull on the projected BOX with the pool's own rx/ry as margin, not on world x alone, because `project()` pinches on depth and lifts z northward, so a world-x test is not a screen test. Remember `drawPuddleLights` runs in the SCREEN pass after `applyLight` and needs the same cull or the two disagree. And carry a SIM FINGERPRINT through the before/after comparison: a `?pause`d page still runs rAF, so a canvas read is unpinned even after a synchronous draw.
